lines.text: Port Murmur, nine in the morning. Usually the gulls, the foghorns and the fish sellers make this the loudest harbor on the coast.
Not today. At midnight the Silence Act took effect, and any street sound over sixty decibels now carries a fine.

lines.speaker: pip
lines.text: (Okay. Nobody's here. One song before the Act notices me.)

lines.speaker: gus
lines.text: Pip, you're playing today? Quick, then, the sad one. My haddock love the sad one.

lines.speaker: pip
lines.text: Um, hi, Gus. Just a quiet one. I put a sock in it.

lines.speaker: pip
lines.text: (There is no sock. There has never been a sock.)
Pip plays the sad one. Three people stop, then ten, and a toddler starts dancing very badly. For a moment, it is a good morning.
A white van mounts the pavement. Three officers in grey step out, decibel meters raised like holy relics.

lines.speaker: hush
lines.text: Quiet Squad! Nobody move, nobody hum. Officer Mute, a reading, please.

lines.speaker: mute
lines.text: Eighty-two decibels, Sergeant. Peaking at eighty-four on the high bit. Velvet Heights will be devastated.

lines.speaker: hush
lines.text: Eighty-four. In a residential zone. Before lunch.

lines.speaker: hush
lines.text: Citizen, under Section 4, Subsection Shh, you are making a sound.

lines.speaker: pip
lines.text: I, um. It's a trumpet. That's sort of its whole job.

lines.speaker: hush
lines.text: Then its job is now illegal. Lower the instrument slowly and surrender it for decibel-safe storage.

lines.speaker: gus
lines.text: Pip. The march is heading north up Main Street. Get in the middle, stay out of their sight lines, and pick up your tips on the way.

lines.speaker: pip
lines.text: (Surrender it? It was Grandad's. Okay, feet, please do something brave.)
